key_insight: SIM-PINN combines projection-based decoupling, iterative coupling, and multi-stage neural networks to improve convergence and accuracy for incompressible Navier–Stokes equations.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets a more accurate mesh-free fluid solver while reducing training difficulties from nonlinearity, coupled constraints, and spectral bias.
method: Split Navier–Stokes into linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations solved by dedicated networks.
Couple the separate solves through projection-based inner iterations.
Refine velocity at targeted frequencies across stages, each corresponding to a projection iteration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence and accuracy on steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flow simulations, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational cost or scalability beyond the two demonstrated flow cases.
paper_title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
